Personalities.Name: The Careful
Personalities.Description: Banks early and takes few risks.

Personalities.Name: The Bold
Personalities.Description: Presses on and spreads catspaws widely.

Personalities.Name: The Closer
Personalities.Description: Chases short tracks and banks the moment one is won.

Fallbacks.Note: Existing residents fill a dispute's lead part when an occupation matches; otherwise a local delegate stands in. Dispute facts never need an occupation the settlement lacks.

Disputes.Silhouette: long shaft with a flat blade

Cast.accused: the helper who left the far bank
Cast.witness: a carrier waiting at the bank

opening: My {prop} is broken and my helper has gone. Who minds the bank, {candidate}?
Nobody answers from the far bank any more. Bring them back, {candidate}.
The crossing stands empty. {candidate}, ask why my helper walked off.
progress: A carrier saw my helper on the far side. That is something.
They are talking about coming back. Not yet, but talking.
The far bank answered my call today.
setback: Not a word from the other bank. I am tying up again.
They said the {prop} was never the trouble. Now I do not know what is.
Wrong question. My helper's door stayed shut.
revisit: The bank is quiet, {candidate}. Come back and ask them again.
Still no crossing. The {prop} will keep; my helper may not.
People wait on the bank and look at me, {candidate}.
agreement: My helper returns and the {prop} gets mended. Thank you, {candidate}.
We spoke at last. The crossing opens and you have my voice, {candidate}.
They take the far bank again. I will vouch for you, {candidate}.
acknowledgement: {lead} has hands on both banks again, thanks to {winner}.
{winner} asked why the helper left, not only when they would return.
The crossing runs because {winner} listened to both banks.

Cast.witness: an elder or householder who remembers the old stakes

opening: This {prop} moved in the night. Whose strip is it? You decide, {candidate}.
Two of us claim the same strip. {candidate}, walk the line with us.
The old stakes are gone and nobody agrees where they stood. Help us, {candidate}.
progress: An elder remembers two of the stakes. We are getting somewhere.
We stood on the same strip and did not shout. A start.
One stake is back where it was. One more to go.
setback: They pulled the stakes up again. I am done talking today.
Words, then more words. The {prop} lies in the grass.
That went badly. Now neither of us will speak.
revisit: Still crooked, {candidate}. Walk it again with us.
The {prop} lies where it fell, and nobody will lift it but you.
Two strips and one quarrel, {candidate}. Come back.
agreement: Straight and fair. {candidate}, I accept the new line.
We shook on it, both of us. You may count on us, {candidate}.
The stakes go back by the elder's word. Thank you, {candidate}.
acknowledgement: No more quarrels over the {prop}. Thanks to {winner}.
{winner} walked the line with {lead}, and it holds.
The boundary stands because {winner} asked who remembered, not who shouted.

Disputes.Silhouette: thin stem with a leafy tuft

Cast.accused: the cutters felling past the marked slope
Cast.witness: a gleaner or shepherd who works the ridge

opening: They fell trees faster than the forest grows. Plant this {prop} with me, {candidate}.
The ridge is bare where the old trees stood. Speak for the young ones, {candidate}.
Someone keeps felling the same slope. {candidate}, help me mark what stays.
progress: A few more saplings are in the ground. The cutters watched.
Someone saw the felling. They are thinking about saying so.
The cutters are slowing down. Keep at it.
setback: The axes were on the slope before dawn. I cannot stop them alone.
They felled the young ones too. Today is lost.
Too hasty. The cutters would not listen and the ridge paid.
revisit: The stumps are still there, {candidate}. So is my {prop}.
Come back and help me guard the young trees.
Another tree fell while you were away, {candidate}.
agreement: We fell one, we plant two. {candidate}, you have my vote.
The ridge will be green again. Thank you, {candidate}.
The slope is marked and the cutters agreed. I am with you, {candidate}.
acknowledgement: The young trees on the ridge are {winner}'s doing.
Because of {winner}, {lead} plants before the felling.
{winner} got the cutters to mark the slope. It shows.

Disputes.Silhouette: long beam with a crack down the middle

Cast.accused: whoever keeps the sound timber back
Cast.witness: a carrier who hauled it and saw where it went

opening: This {prop} will not hold a roof. Someone keeps the good timber back, {candidate}.
Sound wood exists; I saw it stacked. Why is it not here, {candidate}?
I cannot build on a split {prop}. Find who holds the good wood.
progress: A straight plank arrived. Not much, but sound.
A carrier says the good stack sits at the back of a shed. Now we know.
They are loosening their grip. Keep pressing.
setback: The good timber was moved again. I am stuck.
They said there is none. Nobody believes that.
Nothing today. I am setting my tools down.
revisit: The roof is still open to the sky, {candidate}.
Still no sound wood. The {prop} is no better.
I keep asking for timber, {candidate}. Come back with an answer.
agreement: Good wood at last. {candidate} has earned my hands.
The stack is shared out fairly. The roof will stand, {candidate}.
Whoever held it back will let go. I am with you, {candidate}.
acknowledgement: Every sound beam {lead} raises, they owe a little to {winner}.
{winner} found the timber, and the roof stands.
The good wood is shared since {winner} asked where it was kept.

Disputes.Silhouette: round-bellied pot with a narrow neck

Cast.accused: whoever keeps the herb store shut, fearing a shortage
Cast.witness: a gleaner who knows where the herbs grow

opening: My {prop} is dry and the cough is spreading. Who holds the herbs, {candidate}?
There are herbs in this village, just not in my hands. Ask why, {candidate}.
The sick wait on me and I have nothing. Find the herbs, {candidate}.
progress: A few herbs reached me. Thank you.
A gleaner knows where they grow. That helps.
The {prop} is no longer empty. Do not stop.
setback: Someone shut the store on me. Nothing today.
They say herbs are short, but would not show me. Nothing.
Wrong word to the wrong person. The sick must wait.
revisit: Still thin on medicine, {candidate}.
The cough has not eased. Please try again.
My {prop} is as dry as when you left, {candidate}.
agreement: The {prop} will be filled. I stand with {candidate}.
The store opens to the sick first. You have my voice, {candidate}.
Herbs shared, no shortage hidden. Thank you, {candidate}.
acknowledgement: The sick are mending, and {winner} is the reason.
{winner} filled the {prop} for {lead}. People remember that.
Since {winner} spoke up, the herb store opens to anyone ill.

Disputes.Silhouette: wide open container beside the lead

Cast.accused: whoever set a share of grain aside
Cast.witness: a carrier who counted the loads

opening: Look at this {prop}. It was full at the last count. Who took the grain, {candidate}?
Someone sits on a share of grain. {candidate}, help me count it back.
The store is empty and the loads say otherwise. Help me, {candidate}.
progress: A carrier remembers three loads that never reached the store.
The count is closer. Two sacks found.
A share was set aside, they say. A first honest word.
setback: The tally was wrong again. I cannot prove a thing.
They said it spoiled. Nobody saw it spoil.
That frightened them. The grain stays hidden.
revisit: The {prop} is still empty, {candidate}.
Winter is coming and the store holds air. Come back.
Count again with me, {candidate}.
agreement: The grain goes back in the store, shared by need. I accept, {candidate}.
The {prop} will be filled before the cold. You have my voice, {candidate}.
We agreed the count and the share. Thank you, {candidate}.
acknowledgement: The store holds because {winner} made them count out loud.
{lead} sleeps easier since {winner} sat down with the tally.
{winner} brought the missing loads back to the store.

Disputes.Silhouette: T-shaped haft with a heavy head

Cast.accused: the digging crew who walked off
Cast.witness: a carrier who saw which way they went

opening: My {prop} cracked and half the diggers walked off. {candidate}, get them back.
The digging stopped and nobody says why. Will you ask them, {candidate}?
I cannot dig alone with a broken {prop}. Find out where my crew went.
progress: One of them came back for a morning. That counts.
A carrier saw where they went. They are not far.
They say a sound {prop} might bring them back.
setback: They saw me and turned around. Nothing today.
Wrong promise. The digging stays quiet.
They say it was never the {prop}. Then what?
revisit: Still no crew, {candidate}. The stone is not getting softer.
The {prop} lies where it cracked. Come back.
The digging is quiet, {candidate}. Try once more.
agreement: A sound {prop} and the crew returns. Thank you, {candidate}.
They come back, and nobody digs alone again. You have my voice.
The fault was named and mended. I am with you, {candidate}.
acknowledgement: The digging runs again, and {winner} is why.
{winner} asked why the crew left, not when they would be back.
{lead} has hands at the face again thanks to {winner}.

Disputes.Silhouette: slumped sack tied at the neck

opening: This {prop} is mine by the weighing. They say half is theirs. Judge it, {candidate}.
Two of us claim the same {prop}. Who owns what came off the field, {candidate}?
We both counted the {prop}, and counted differently. Help us, {candidate}.
progress: Someone saw it weighed. They will say what they saw.
We agree on the weight at least.
They gave up a handful. It is a start.
setback: Now they say I owe them a debt as well. This is worse.
No agreement. Each took a side of the {prop}.
The weighing was disputed. We start again.
revisit: The {prop} sits between us, {candidate}.
Half each, all mine, or all theirs. Help us choose.
Still no shares settled, {candidate}.
agreement: Shares agreed and cut in notches for all to see. Thank you, {candidate}.
We split it by the weighing. I accept, {candidate}.
Fair shares, and both of us said so. You have my voice.
acknowledgement: The {prop} was split fairly. {winner} did that.
{lead} and their neighbour trade grain again, thanks to {winner}.
{winner} had them agree the weighing before the sharing.

Disputes.Silhouette: open vessel with a curved handle

Cast.witness: a carrier who fills first at dawn

opening: My {prop} comes up half empty. Someone draws past their turn, {candidate}.
The water runs low and everyone blames me. Help me, {candidate}.
There is water, but not where it is needed. Who keeps taking it, {candidate}?
progress: A carrier saw who fills first at dawn. That helps.
The {prop} came up fuller today. Not full.
They agreed to wait their turn. For now.
setback: Someone took it all before dawn. Nothing left.
I blamed the wrong person. Now nobody will answer me.
The {prop} came up empty. They shrugged.
revisit: The water is lower, {candidate}. Come back.
My {prop} is still half empty. People notice.
The queue grows, {candidate}. Please try again.
agreement: Turns and shares, fair to all. {candidate}, thank you.
The {prop} will come up full again. You have my voice, {candidate}.
We keep a count of turns now. I am with you, {candidate}.
acknowledgement: Nobody goes thirsty, and {winner} is why.
{winner} had them take turns. {lead} says it works.
The water is shared since {winner} spoke up.

Disputes.Silhouette: round disc stood on its edge

Cast.accused: whoever broke the wheel on the road
Cast.witness: the bystander who saw it and will not say

opening: My {prop} broke on the road and someone saw how. They will not say, {candidate}.
A witness stares at their feet. Help me ask kindly, {candidate}.
Somebody saw who cracked my {prop}. Silence helps no one, {candidate}.
progress: The witness said a little. Not the name, but a little.
They will talk if no one shames them. That is something.
A carrier says the witness wants to speak. They need a reason.
setback: The witness bolted. I pushed too hard.
Now nobody saw anything. Wrong words, wrong moment.
Shouted at in public. They will not speak now.
revisit: Still no word from the witness, {candidate}.
My {prop} is still broken and still unexplained.
Try again, gently, {candidate}.
agreement: The witness spoke and no one is shamed. {candidate}, thank you.
It was an accident, it seems, and the {prop} gets mended. You have my voice.
What was seen is told. I am satisfied, {candidate}.
acknowledgement: The truth about the {prop} came out because {winner} was gentle.
{winner} let the witness speak when ready. {lead} remembers.
Nobody fears speaking up now. {winner} did that.

Disputes.Silhouette: slim rolled bar held in one hand

Cast.wronged: reeve or chief, keeper of the record (lead)
Cast.witness: an elder who remembers when it was made

opening: Two folk hold this {prop} and swear it names them. Judge it, {candidate}.
The {prop} says one thing, the elders another. Whose land is it, {candidate}?
I keep the record, and the record is disputed. I need your word, {candidate}.
progress: An elder remembers when it was made. That settles part.
The marks are clearer by daylight. We read it together.
Both sides agreed to hear the elder out.
setback: They tugged at the {prop} itself. Now nobody trusts it.
Both left angry. The record stays unread.
The elder would not speak before them. Nothing today.
revisit: The {prop} lies unread, {candidate}. The quarrel does not.
Still two claims and one record. Come back.
Land does not wait forever, {candidate}.
agreement: The {prop} is read aloud and both accept it. Thank you, {candidate}.
The claim is settled and the record kept. You have my voice, {candidate}.
Both have their share in the record now. I am with you, {candidate}.
acknowledgement: The record stands because {winner} had it read aloud.
{lead} keeps the {prop} safe, and {winner} made it matter.
{winner} made both claimants hear the elder. It held.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Old fisher
ListeningLines.Text: The path floods every morning and nobody lifts a spade.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Young shepherd
ListeningLines.Text: I mended that fence twice this moon and the goats still get through.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Weaver
ListeningLines.Text: My share is smaller than last month and nobody tells me why.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Carrier
ListeningLines.Text: I hauled all that and got a nod. A nod does not fill a basket.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Potter
ListeningLines.Text: My roof leaks and I have asked three times.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Gleaner
ListeningLines.Text: The berries were picked clean before I woke. Fair?

ListeningLines.Speaker: Woodcutter
ListeningLines.Text: The felling is loud and the stumps are everywhere.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Householder
ListeningLines.Text: The talk goes round and round while the fire burns low.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Storekeeper
ListeningLines.Text: Everyone counts the grain. Nobody counts who carried it.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Farmer
ListeningLines.Text: The strip beside mine keeps shrinking and nobody will say why.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Baker
ListeningLines.Text: Someone borrows my paddle and never brings it back.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Quarrier
ListeningLines.Text: Half my crew went off and I am told to mind the stone.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Warden
ListeningLines.Text: I walk the fence all night and hear complaints all day.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Elder
ListeningLines.Text: Nobody asks the old ones what the old stakes looked like.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Net mender
ListeningLines.Text: You can do this. One more try and it will hold.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Potter
ListeningLines.Text: That was well said. Keep your voice steady.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Old fisher
ListeningLines.Text: Well done, friend. The hard part is behind you.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Young shepherd
ListeningLines.Text: Do not stop now. The hill is nearly climbed.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Midwife
ListeningLines.Text: I believe in you. Take your time.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Curer
ListeningLines.Text: Everyone starts clumsy. Look how far you have come.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Stonecutter
ListeningLines.Text: Your work gets better every day. People notice.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Farmer
ListeningLines.Text: Stand tall. They listen when you speak like that.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Carrier
ListeningLines.Text: You are stronger than you think. Lift it with me.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Gleaner
ListeningLines.Text: Good effort. The next one will be better.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Storekeeper
ListeningLines.Text: Keep going. The whole village is behind you.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Child
ListeningLines.Text: You were so close! Try again, I know you can.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Sawyer
ListeningLines.Text: Steady hands. Cut it once, cut it true.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Elder
ListeningLines.Text: You listened first and spoke second. That is rare.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Weaver
ListeningLines.Text: Careful on the ice. It cracks when you least expect it.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Old fisher
ListeningLines.Text: Keep off the marsh at dusk. The ground gives way.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Potter
ListeningLines.Text: Mind the old beam. It is split and could come down.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Baker
ListeningLines.Text: Keep the fire away from the thatch or we lose the lot.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Net mender
ListeningLines.Text: Watch the river. It rises fast after rain.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Young shepherd
ListeningLines.Text: Wolves near the ridge. Stay together tonight.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Curer
ListeningLines.Text: Those berries are bitter and make you sick. Leave them.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Storekeeper
ListeningLines.Text: Do not trust a bargain that sounds too good.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Woodcutter
ListeningLines.Text: A tree is leaning on the slope. Keep clear.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Gleaner
ListeningLines.Text: Do not lean on that rail. The rope is rotten.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Quarrier
ListeningLines.Text: Loose stone above the path. Walk wide.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Carrier
ListeningLines.Text: Take care on the log. It is wet and it rolls.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Warden
ListeningLines.Text: Quarrels in the dark end in blood. Talk by daylight.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Elder
ListeningLines.Text: A rumour grows faster than a weed. Do not feed it.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Farmer
ListeningLines.Text: Do not worry. The grain will last until the harvest.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Gleaner
ListeningLines.Text: It is all right. Nobody blames you for the spilled water.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Weaver
ListeningLines.Text: There is plenty for everyone, I promise.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Old fisher
ListeningLines.Text: Relax. The storm has passed and the roof held.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Potter
ListeningLines.Text: No harm done. We can mend it by morning.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Net mender
ListeningLines.Text: The child is safe, asleep by the fire.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Young shepherd
ListeningLines.Text: You are not alone. We will manage together.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Midwife
ListeningLines.Text: It will heal. The wound is clean and shallow.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Baker
ListeningLines.Text: Everything is in hand. Rest now.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Storekeeper
ListeningLines.Text: The count is honest. Nothing is hidden.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Curer
ListeningLines.Text: The fire is out and the camp is safe.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Stonecutter
ListeningLines.Text: Calm yourself. The lost goat is wandering back.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Carrier
ListeningLines.Text: It looks worse than it is. A little clay will mend it.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Elder
ListeningLines.Text: Whoever spoke out of turn will be heard out, not shamed.

ListeningLines.Speaker: Carrier
ListeningLines.Text: Where did you leave the good flint knife?

ListeningLines.Speaker: Weaver
ListeningLines.Text: Who will cut the reeds this season?

ListeningLines.Speaker: Curer
ListeningLines.Text: Has anyone seen the traders on the river road?

ListeningLines.Speaker: Gleaner
ListeningLines.Text: How much grain is left in the store?

ListeningLines.Speaker: Stonecutter
ListeningLines.Text: Why did the elders move the boundary stones?

ListeningLines.Speaker: Net mender
ListeningLines.Text: When does the crossing open again?

ListeningLines.Speaker: Young shepherd
ListeningLines.Text: Which path leads to the high pasture?

ListeningLines.Speaker: Old fisher
ListeningLines.Text: Do you know who borrowed the big pot?

ListeningLines.Speaker: Potter
ListeningLines.Text: What did the healer say about the cough?

ListeningLines.Speaker: Farmer
ListeningLines.Text: Are we sharing the catch or trading it?

ListeningLines.Speaker: Woodcutter
ListeningLines.Text: Who marked this slope, and who unmarked it?

ListeningLines.Speaker: Storekeeper
ListeningLines.Text: Who saw the loads come in, and who saw them go?

ListeningLines.Speaker: Baker
ListeningLines.Text: Did you hear the horn from the hill last night?

ListeningLines.Speaker: Warden
ListeningLines.Text: Whose turn is it to mind the fire?
